text.intro:
Where the existing-data FTIR EC investigation stands on 9 Nov 2026, after the 7 Nov closeout, for the end-of-December
check-in with the supervisor. A status page, not a recorded meeting: every chart reads an export that already exists
(the closeout source scoreboard and saved Addis fits, the 9 Oct and 28 Oct meeting bundles, and the repository history).
Source scores are µg per filter on 12,386 common IMPROVE filters; Addis comparisons are µg/m³ against optical comparators.
text.domain:
**Addis is outside what the IMPROVE library has seen.** In µg/m³ the Addis median is
41× the IMPROVE median; per filter, which is what FTIR sees, it is
9×, and 78 % of Addis filters are still above the IMPROVE
99th percentile. EC is 19–24 % of Addis PM2.5 by season against about 4 % across the
IMPROVE library. A calibration cannot be checked on a composition it never trained on.
text.preprocess:
**Baseline correction is the largest single improvement, and it is not a fix.** Against HIPS optical BC
(MAC 10), the SPARTAN published product has intercept -6.17 µg/m³ and slope 2.31 (n = 189);
the spline-baselined calibration moves that to -1.37 and 0.68 (n = 233).

**The aethalometer does not separate the candidates.** Against it, most intercepts are already near zero (published
+0.08, PTFE-anchored VIBES +0.10; production VIBES
-0.95 µg/m³), while HIPS optical BC against the same aethalometer has intercept
+2.84 (n = 172). Which measurement carries the offset stays open: agreement between optical
methods is a diagnostic, **not** proof of correct EC, and no Addis filter has thermal (TOR) EC.
text.seasons:
**The seasons fail differently.** With the same baseline-corrected all-IMPROVE calibration the Addis slope is
0.31 in Dry, 0.49 in Belg and 0.50 in Kiremt. Choosing each season's own spectral
look-alikes lifts Kiremt to 0.94 but leaves Dry at 0.35 and Belg at 0.32, and no other
choice of calibration filters (lowest OC/EC, urban IMPROVE) brings Dry or Belg near 1. Per µg of EC, Addis carries far less
organic absorbance than its IMPROVE look-alikes, least in Dry: the likely cause is **composition, not concentration**.
text.scores:
**No universal winner.** Six preprocessing pipelines, the same 12,386 IMPROVE filters, 18 PLS components and
five site-grouped folds, every eligible filter predicted. Lowest median absolute error: Spline baseline; lowest
mean absolute error and 95th percentile error: PTFE-anchored VIBES; lowest RMSE: Raw spectra. EPO moves the 163 heavy,
low-OC/EC IMPROVE filters toward 1:1 (median FTIR/TOR 0.78 → 0.90) at the cost of overall error
(MAE 1.70 → 1.84 µg/filter). Descriptive differences, not significance tests; prior exploratory settings mean this is
a retrospective comparison, not independent model selection.
text.time:
**The analysis is closed; the writing has not started.** 461 commits since 5 Oct, 261 of them in the week of
Oct 26, almost all analysis, gallery and release work. The repository holds no manuscript draft: `manuscript/` has citation tooling only. The supervisor's definition of finished is the
**chapter written and the paper ready**, so the next six weeks go to writing.
text.next:
**Proposed position for the December–January decision: a defensible pathway exists.** Write paper 1 on the
existing-data result now: why an IMPROVE-trained FTIR EC calibration does not transfer to Addis, how much preprocessing and
cohort choice recover, the seasonal structure, and the compositional explanation, with absolute accuracy stated as the open
limit. The incoming Addis TOR filters then become the validation step, not a prerequisite. Agree what agreement would count as
evidence before they arrive.

Open analysis from the AAAR list (OC/EC-selected cohorts for Dry and Belg, the dust band, a season-specific MAC, optical pyrolysis
on dark IMPROVE filters) waits until the draft exists or goes to future work. The next objective (Brian's glacier black carbon
project, international collaborations across SPARTAN/MAIA, or the PurpleAir objective the committee still expects) is chosen in January.
